name: Dental cleaning / scale and polish

lead: A scale and polish removes tartar and plaque and polishes the teeth. People book it to lift stain from tobacco, tea, coffee and red wine, so teeth look cleaner and lighter right after the visit, and as a first step before whitening.

Ultrasonic or hand scalers remove tartar, then the surfaces are polished. Whitening is a separate process aimed mainly at stain inside the tooth. Wikipedia notes polishing removes only some plaque and stain and does not remove calculus.

paras: It is a routine appointment with a hygienist, often every six to twelve months. Deeper scaling and root planing is a gum-disease treatment that also smooths exposed root surfaces.

Cited concerns include root sensitivity after root planing, damage from ultrasonic scaling to enamel cracks, early caries and resin restorations, and aerosols from ultrasonic scalers. A 2018 Cochrane review found little to no difference for adults without severe periodontitis between scaling and polishing and no scheduled care.

Routine scale and polish for periodontal health in adults
Routine Scale and Polish for Periodontal Health in Adults

angle.text: A hygienist scale and polish lifts tartar and surface stain, so teeth look cleaner and lighter right after the visit. It is often the first step before whitening, since whitening targets stain inside the tooth.

lead: Dental cleaning, often called scale and polish, is professional removal of plaque, calculus (tartar) and surface stain from the teeth by a dental hygienist or dentist. A regular cleaning includes scaling and polishing but not root planing, which is part of deeper gum treatment [1].

Wikipedia describes polishing as removing only some plaque and stain, not calculus, so it is paired with scaling [1]. Surface (extrinsic) stains from tobacco, tannin-rich drinks, plaque and calculus can be removed by professional prophylaxis, while whitening targets intrinsic stain [2].

A 2018 Cochrane review of scaling and polishing found little to no difference for adults without severe periodontitis compared with no scheduled care, while other reviews have been inconclusive or addressed scaling and root planing for periodontitis [1].
infobox: Ultrasonic or sonic scalers, hand instruments, polishing

paras: Scaling uses ultrasonic or sonic scalers, which act by cavitation and liquid flow, and hand instruments such as scalers and curettes [1]. In deeper treatment, called scaling and root planing, the area is numbed and root surfaces are smoothed, with maintenance visits generally recommended every three to four months for periodontal patients [1].
Wikipedia's tooth whitening article states that professional prophylaxis or micro-abrasion can remove extrinsic stains and that dentists or hygienists clean the teeth before in-office bleaching [2].

Root planing can damage the root surface and cause sensitivity [1]. A 2018 study cited by Wikipedia found ultrasonic scaling can damage enamel cracks, early caries and resin restorations, and ultrasonic scalers create aerosols that can spread pathogens [1].

Evidence concerns periodontal outcomes rather than appearance. A 2018 Cochrane review of scaling and polishing found little to no difference for adults without severe periodontitis compared with no scheduled care, a 2015 British Dental Association review was inconclusive, and a 2016 Canadian review found reduced plaque and gingival index improvement with scaling and root planing at three and six months [1]. No studies of scale and polish specifically for cosmetic outcomes were located.
